parsed.main_gap: The central Lemma (that σ(x)=P(x)∩Q is good for every term x) — the entire difficulty of the problem — is asserted with "details omitted" and never proved.

errors.description: The key lemma, which is the crux of the problem (showing primes larger than a_1 are irrelevant to the compatibility condition), is stated without proof; 'standard' is unjustified and the referenced repair construction R p^k never appears in the argument.
errors.quote: **Proof.** Induction over the sequence terms in increasing order (standard; details omitted). \(\square\)

errors.description: The write-up admits the lemma is only supported by numerical experiments, which earn no credit; the claim that the argument 'proves it independently' is false since no argument is given.
errors.quote: These computations only test the lemma; the argument above proves it independently.

errors.description: Minor: the final step asserts every length-L interval in [A,∞) contains exactly T terms via 'each residue modulo L once'; this needs (4) applied to the residue-class characterization, stated but not spelled out (repairable).
errors.quote: Every interval of \(L\) consecutive integers contained in \([A,\infty)\) contains each residue modulo \(L\) once and therefore contains exactly \(T\) sequence terms, by (4).

parsed.notes: The surrounding framework (characterization (1), upward-closed goodness, periodicity mod ∏_{p≤A} p, and the counting argument) is correct and cleanly done, but it is only a reduction; the essential lemma is missing entirely.
